blocks.text: Testing and debugging are essential to make sure an application works correctly in all conditions. They find and remove errors before the software is released; regular testing prevents unexpected failures during use, and debugging locates the cause of an error and fixes it. Together they increase reliability and user confidence.

blocks.title: Class activity
blocks.text: Discuss situations where errors cause failures, and explain why testing is important.

Testing checks whether an application meets its requirements and that every function gives correct results. It reduces the risk of crashes or wrong output, and it confirms that changes have not broken features that already worked. Thoroughly tested applications are more trustworthy and stable.

blocks.caption: Types of program error
rows: The code breaks the language's rules, so the program does not run at all
if x > 5 without the colon: SyntaxError
An invalid operation happens while the program runs, and it stops
a = 10; b = 0; result = a / b gives ZeroDivisionError
The program runs but gives the wrong result
area = length + width instead of length * width
Data errors (wrong or badly formatted data) and resource leaks (files or connections never closed)
A file left open uses memory until the program ends

blocks.alt: Three panels with short code. Logic error: length = 5, width = 3, area = length + width (highlighted), print(area) gives 8; it runs but the answer is wrong; fix area = length * width (15). Runtime error: a = 10, b = 0, result = a / b (highlighted); it stops while running with ZeroDivisionError. Syntax error: x = 7, if x > 5 (highlighted, missing colon), print; it will not run at all: SyntaxError.
blocks.caption: Logic, runtime and syntax errors (original diagram after Fig 5.1).
blocks.long_description: Python reports syntax and runtime errors itself, but it cannot know that a formula is wrong; only testing the results catches logic errors.

blocks.prompt: A program to average two marks prints 140 for marks 60 and 80. Which kind of error is this, and what is the likely fix?
blocks.explanation: A logic error: the program runs but the result is wrong. It probably computes the sum and does not divide by 2; the fix is average = (a + b) / 2, which gives 70.

items: Testing finds errors before release and checks that changes break nothing.
Syntax errors stop the program running; runtime errors stop it mid-way; logic errors give wrong results.
Other bugs: data errors, resource leaks.
